worked_example.problem: A tick sucks blood from a dog, and the dog becomes weak. What type of interaction is this?
steps: The tick gains food; the dog is harmed.
One lives on another and harms it: parasitism. The tick is the parasite and the dog is the host.

cards.idea: Predation: a predator kills and eats its prey. Parasitism: a parasite lives on or in a host and harms it.
example: A snake eating a frog is predation; a tapeworm in the gut is parasitism.

cards.idea: Mutualism: both gain. Commensalism: one gains, the other is not harmed. Competition: both need the same scarce thing.
example: Bees and flowers both gain: mutualism.

cards.idea: Animals help plants reproduce: insects pollinate flowers and animals spread seeds.
example: Birds eat fruits and drop the seeds far away.

check.prompt: How do bees help flowering plants reproduce?

right.text: They carry pollen from flower to flower.

wrong.explain: Bees collect nectar and pollen; they carry pollen between flowers.

wrong.text: They kill pests in the soil.

questions.prompt: Match each type of interaction with an example.

pool.right: one animal kills and eats another: an owl and a rat
one lives on or in another and harms it: a tick on a dog
both gain: bees get nectar and the flowers are pollinated
both need the same thing that is in short supply: weeds and maize for water and light
one gains and the other is not harmed: an orchid growing on a tree branch

pick.t: A leopard kills and eats an antelope.
pick.why: Predation: A leopard kills and eats an antelope.

pick.t: Mosquitoes suck human blood and can spread malaria.
pick.why: Parasitism: Mosquitoes suck human blood and can spread malaria.

pick.t: Bacteria in bean root nodules get food; the bean plant gets nitrogen.
pick.why: Mutualism: Bacteria in bean root nodules get food; the bean plant gets nitrogen.

pick.t: Weeds and cassava both need the same water and light.
pick.why: Competition: Weeds and cassava both need the same water and light.

pick.t: A fern grows on a palm trunk without harming the palm.
pick.why: Commensalism: A fern grows on a palm trunk without harming the palm.

questions.prompt: Why do farmers remove weeds from a maize farm?

right.text: Weeds compete with the maize for water, light and minerals.

wrong.explain: Weeds compete; they do not eat the maize.

wrong.text: Weeds give the maize more water.

wrong.explain: Weeds compete; they do not live on the maize.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: A predator kills and eats its prey.

wrong.text: Competition happens when there is more than enough for all.
wrong.explain: Competition happens when something is in short supply.
